title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON MANAGEMENT OF FIREFIGHTING EQUIPMENT
full_text:
■ Enforcement Decree of the Act on Management of Firefighting Equipment [Attached Table 2] <Amended on May 15, 2023>

Detailed Criteria for Revocation of Designation or Suspension of Services of Certification Institutions (Re: Article 21 (2))

1. General criteria

(a) Where there are two or more violations and the respective disposition criteria differ, the heavier disposition criteria shall apply. Where two or more disposition criteria all provide for suspension of services, the heavier suspension period shall be increased by up to one half, within a period not exceeding the sum of the respective suspension periods.

(b) Administrative disposition criteria according to the number of violations shall apply where an administrative disposition has been imposed for the same violation within the preceding two years. The period shall be calculated by reference to the date on which the administrative disposition was imposed for the violation and the date on which the same violation committed again after that disposition was detected.

(c) Where an aggravated administrative disposition is imposed under item (b), the occurrence level applied for the aggravated disposition shall be the level immediately following the occurrence level of the administrative disposition imposed before the violation (where two or more administrative dispositions were imposed within the period under item (b), the highest such occurrence level).

(d) The disposition authority may aggravate or mitigate a disposition in consideration of the following circumstances concerning the motive, substance and number of violations, etc. Where the disposition is suspension of services, it may be aggravated or mitigated by up to one half of the prescribed standard. Revocation of designation may be mitigated to suspension of services for six months (excluding cases falling under Article 14 (6) 1 or 7 of the Act).

1) Grounds for aggravation

(a) Where the violation is found to have resulted from intent or gross negligence, rather than minor carelessness or a simple error;

(b) Where the substance and degree of the violation are found to cause substantial harm to persons seeking certification of fire equipment and users of fire equipment;

(c) Where aggravation is deemed necessary in light of the duration of the violation, the number of administrative dispositions received, etc.

2) Grounds for mitigation

(a) Where the violation is found to have resulted from minor carelessness or a simple error, rather than intent or gross negligence;

(b) Where the substance and degree of the violation are minor and it is deemed capable of immediate correction.

2. Individual criteria

| Violation | Legal basis | First violation | Second violation | Third or subsequent violation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Obtaining designation as a certification institution by fraud or other improper means | Article 14 (6) 1 of the Act | Revocation of designation | | |
| (b) Failing to perform certification services for a continuous period of one year or longer without good cause | Article 14 (6) 2 of the Act | Suspension of services for one month | Suspension of services for two months | Suspension of services for three months |
| (c) Ceasing to meet the requirements for designation as a certification institution under Article 14 (1) of the Act | Article 14 (6) 3 of the Act | Suspension of services for three months | Suspension of services for six months | Revocation of designation |
| (d) Being deemed to have lost public confidence in certification due to errors, omissions, etc. | Article 14 (6) 4 of the Act | Suspension of services for one month | Suspension of services for two months | Suspension of services for three months |
| (e) Refusing an application for certification of fire equipment without good cause | Article 14 (6) 5 of the Act | Suspension of services for one month | Suspension of services for two months | Suspension of services for three months |
| (f) Engaging in improper conduct in relation to certification | Article 14 (6) 6 of the Act | Suspension of services for three months | Suspension of services for six months | Revocation of designation |
| (g) Performing certification services during a suspension period in violation of an order to suspend all or part of the services | Article 14 (6) 7 of the Act | Revocation of designation | | |
